tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

The user is describing an issue with their merge tool (merge-forge, which is the working directory /Users/alden/Desktop/dev/merge-forge). They want to optimize a specific behavior: when accepting one side, the per-word diff highlights are lost, so they can't see the changes to combine both sides.

The user's request is in Vietnamese. Let me translate:

"This merge tool is not yet optimized at one point: In image 1, when neither side is accepted, both sides show per-word diff as: 1: flex, flex-col; 2: 6xl, lg... but when I accept the left side into center, it loses the highlight of those diff words. Is there a way to optimize this spot so that when I accept one side, it still keeps the per-word highlight so I know the change point to merge/combine both."

So the issue: The merge tool shows a 3-pane merge view (left, center/result, right). When you accept a side into the center, the per-word diff highlighting disappears from the center pane. The user wants the per-word highlighting to persist so they can still see what changed when they later want to combine both sides.

Let me explore the codebase to understand the architecture.

58:   chunks: readonly Chunk[],
59:   centerRanges: ReadonlyMap<number, CenterRange>,
60:   totals: LineTotals,

64:   let centerCursor = 0;
65:   let rightCursor = 0;

70:     const stable = chunk.left.start - leftCursor;

73:         left: stable,
74:         center: Math.max(0, center.start - centerCursor),
75:         right: stable,
76:         startLeft: leftCursor,
77:         startCenter: centerCursor,
78:         startRight: rightCursor,
79:       });
80:       leftCursor += stable;
81:       centerCursor = center.start;
82:       rightCursor += stable;
83:     }
84:     segments.push({
85:       left: chunk.left.end - chunk.left.start,
86:       center: center.end - center.start,
87:       right: chunk.right.end - chunk.right.start,
88:       startLeft: chunk.left.start,
89:       startCenter: center.start,
90:       startRight: chunk.right.start,

115:  * the 1-based base line as a string out — or `'·'` for lines inside a chunk, where
116:  * the base text has been replaced and no original number exists.

119:  * the mapping is a running offset; each chunk shifts it by (base span − center span).

140:       }

143:       }
144:       centerCursor = row.center.end;
145:       baseCursor = row.baseEnd;
146:     }

149:   };

153: export interface PixelExtent {
154:   top: number;
155:   bottom: number;
156: }

160:  * lines, or its padding zone's full span when it has none.
161:  *

163:  * for `own > 0` pass the *top of the first content line*; for `own === 0` pass the
164:  * *bottom of the line the zone follows* (or the document top for a zone above line 0).
165:  * `computeSpacers` gives an empty side a zone of `maxLines`, so that is the empty span.
166:  */

168:   ownLines: number,
169:   maxLines: number,
170:   anchor: number,
171:   lineHeight: number,

174:   return { top: anchor, bottom: anchor + span };

180:   afterLine: number;
181:   heightInLines: number;
182:   /** Colour family of the chunk this padding stands in for; stable gaps carry none. */
183:   visual?: ChunkVisual;

188:  * lines in all three panes. Equal heights are what let scroll sync be a plain 1:1 mirror
189:  * instead of an interpolation.
190:  */
191: export function computeSpacers(segments: readonly Segment[]): Record<PaneName, Spacer[]> {
192:   const spacers: Record<PaneName, Spacer[]> = { left: [], center: [], right: [] };
193:   for (const segment of segments) {
194:     const tallest = Math.max(segment.left, segment.center, segment.right);
195:     const rows: Array<[PaneName, number, number]> = [
196:       ['left', segment.left, segment.startLeft],
197:       ['center', segment.center, segment.startCenter],
198:       ['right', segment.right, segment.startRight],
199:     ];
200:     for (const [pane, own, start] of rows) {
201:       const missing = tallest - own;
202:       if (missing > 0) {
203:         const spacer: Spacer = { afterLine: start + own, heightInLines: missing };
204:         if (segment.visual) {
205:           spacer.visual = segment.visual;
206:         }
207:         spacers[pane].push(spacer);
208:       }
209:     }
210:   }
211:   return spacers;
212: }

11: /**

19: /** Chunk states and tracker positions as they were at one exact text version. */
20: interface Snapshot {
21:   states: {
22:     state: Chunk['state'];
23:     dismissedLeft: boolean;
24:     dismissedRight: boolean;
25:   }[];

29: export class ChunkStore {

31:   private readonly trackers = new Map<number, string>();
32:   /**

34:    * version id — Monaco's id that comes back to the same value when undo/redo lands on
35:    * byte-identical text. Text edits are on Monaco's undo stack but chunk states are not,
36:    * so this is what lets Cmd+Z restore the whole UI, not just the characters.
37:    */

43:   constructor(

58:   }

60:   /** Detaches from the editor so a new store can take over (whitespace-mode rebuild). */
61:   dispose(): void {
62:     this.contentListener?.dispose();
63:     this.model.deltaDecorations([...this.trackers.values()], []);

65:     this.history.clear();
66:   }

68:   private snapshot(): void {
69:     this.history.set(this.model.getAlternativeVersionId(), {
70:       states: this.chunks.map((chunk) => ({

72:         dismissedLeft: chunk.dismissedLeft,

121:   };
122:   applySpacers(
123:     panes,
124:     computeSpacers(computeSegments(chunks, centerRanges, totals)),
125:     session.zoneIds,
126:   );
127:   renderDecorations(
128:     chunks,
129:     centerRanges,
130:     session.collections,
131:     session.highlight === 'words' ? session.wordRanges : undefined,
132:     {
133:       currentChunkId: session.currentChunkId,
134:       flashChunkId: session.flashChunkId,
135:       hoverChunkId: session.hoverChunkId,
136:     },
137:   );
138:   redrawConnectors();
139:   updateBaseLineNumbers(centerRanges);
140:   const currentPosition = chunks.findIndex((c) => c.id === session!.currentChunkId);
141:   session.toolbar.update(chunks, currentPosition >= 0 ? currentPosition + 1 : undefined);
142:   // WebStorm's completion card: floats over the result once nothing needs deciding,
143:   // and disappears again the moment any chunk reopens (e.g. via undo).
144:   const allProcessed = chunks.length > 0 && chunks.every((c) => c.state !== 'initial');
145:   session.layout.doneCard.classList.toggle('mf-hidden', !allProcessed);
146:   postState();
147: }

149: /**
150:  * JetBrains shows the original (base) line number next to the current one in the
151:  * result pane. Rebuilding the renderer forces a margin repaint, so it only happens
152:  * when a chunk's mapping actually moved — not on hover or flash refreshes.
153:  */
154: function updateBaseLineNumbers(centerRanges: ReadonlyMap<number, { start: number; end: number }>) {
155:   if (!session) {
156:     return;
157:   }
158:   const signature = session.chunks
159:     .map((chunk) => {
160:       const range = centerRanges.get(chunk.id);
161:       return `${chunk.id}:${chunk.base.start}-${chunk.base.end}:${range?.start}-${range?.end}`;
162:     })
163:     .join(',');
164:   if (signature === lineNumbersSignature) {
165:     return;
166:   }
167:   lineNumbersSignature = signature;
168:   const baseTotal = splitLines(session.payload.base).length;
169:   const baseFor = baseLineNumbers(session.chunks, centerRanges, baseTotal);
170:   session.panes.center.updateOptions({
171:     lineNumbersMinChars: 7,
172:     lineNumbers: (lineNumber: number) => {
173:       const base = baseFor(lineNumber);
174:       return base === '' ? String(lineNumber) : `${base} ${lineNumber}`;
175:     },
176:   });
177: }

363: /** Moves to the next or previous unresolved change and centers it in every pane. */
364: function navigate(direction: 1 | -1): void {
365:   if (!session || session.chunks.length === 0) {
366:     return;
367:   }
368:   const { chunks, panes, store } = session;
369:   const candidates = chunks.filter((c) => c.state === 'initial');
370:   const pool = candidates.length > 0 ? candidates : chunks;
371:   cursor = (cursor + direction + pool.length) % pool.length;
372:   const chunk = pool[cursor];
373:   if (!chunk) {
374:     return;
375:   }
376:   const centerRange = store.centerRange(chunk.id);
377:   // ScrollType.Smooth (0) lets the eye follow the jump; the arrival flash marks the
378:   // destination, then the chunk keeps its "current" outline until the next jump.
379:   const SMOOTH = 0;
380:   panes.center.revealLineInCenter(centerRange.start + 1, SMOOTH);
381:   panes.left.revealLineInCenter(chunk.left.start + 1, SMOOTH);
382:   panes.right.revealLineInCenter(chunk.right.start + 1, SMOOTH);
383:   session.currentChunkId = chunk.id;
384:   session.flashChunkId = chunk.id;
385:   window.clearTimeout(flashTimer);
386:   flashTimer = window.setTimeout(() => {
387:     if (session) {
388:       session.flashChunkId = undefined;
389:       refresh();
390:     }
391:   }, 750);
392:   refresh();
393: }

395: /** Advances to the next pending chunk, or stays put when nothing is left to decide. */
396: function navigateToNextUnresolved(): void {
397:   if (session?.chunks.some((chunk) => chunk.state === 'initial')) {
398:     navigate(1);
399:   }
400: }

402: /**
403:  * Runs a resolution action and, when it settles the chunk, hops to the next pending one
404:  * — accept, accept, accept down the file without reaching for the mouse.
405:  */
406: function resolveAndAdvance(run: () => void, chunkId: number): void {
407:   run();
408:   const chunk = session?.chunks.find((c) => c.id === chunkId);
409:   if (chunk && chunk.state !== 'initial') {
410:     navigateToNextUnresolved();
411:   }
412: }

414: /**
415:  * Applies every change only one side made. Strictly non-conflicting: a conflict —
416:  * including two sides inserting different versions of the same new code — never has an
417:  * automatic answer, and concatenating "both added" variants duplicates real functions
418:  * (found in the field). Red stays red until a human decides.
419:  */
420: function applyAllSafe(): number {
421:   return session?.store.applyMany((chunk) => nonConflictingAction(chunk)) ?? 0;
422: }

424: /**
425:  * "Fix all with AI": the whole file in one click. Non-conflicting changes are applied
426:  * mechanically (deterministic, byte-exact — no reason to ask a model); only the red
427:  * conflicts go to the AI. The drawer report combines both counts.
428:  */
429: let fixAllMechanical = 0;
430: function fixAllWithAi(): void {
431:   if (!session) {
432:     return;
433:   }
434:   const mechanical = applyAllSafe();
435:   const conflictsLeft = session.chunks.some((c) => c.kind === 'conflict' && c.state === 'initial');
436:   if (conflictsLeft) {
437:     fixAllMechanical = mechanical;
438:     requestAiResolve();
439:   }
440:   // No conflicts: the wand already settled everything; the done card takes it from here.
441: }

443: function runAction(action: MergeAction): void {
444:   if (!session) {
445:     return;
446:   }
447:   switch (action) {
448:     case 'nextChange':
449:       navigate(1);
450:       break;
451:     case 'prevChange':
452:       navigate(-1);
453:       break;
454:     case 'applyAllNonConflicting':
455:       applyAllSafe();
456:       break;
457:     case 'requestApply':
458:       requestApply();
459:       break;
460:   }
461: }

470: /**
471:  * The unresolved conflicts (base + both sides) as an AI request, or undefined when none.
472:  * With `onlyChunkId`, a single-conflict request — the ✦ menu's scope — keeping the
473:  * chunk's position-based number so headings match the whole-file numbering.
474:  */
475: function buildAiRequest(onlyChunkId?: number): ExplainRequest | undefined {
476:   if (!session) {
477:     return undefined;
478:   }
479:   const { payload } = session;
480:   const unresolved = session.chunks.filter((c) => c.kind === 'conflict' && c.state === 'initial');
481:   const conflicts =
482:     onlyChunkId === undefined ? unresolved : unresolved.filter((c) => c.id === onlyChunkId);
483:   if (conflicts.length === 0) {
484:     return undefined;
485:   }
486:   return {
487:     filePath: payload.filePath,
488:     languageId: payload.languageId,
489:     labels: payload.labels,
490:     // The current result document — the model's rich baseline around the conflicts.
491:     resultText: session.store.result(),
492:     conflicts: conflicts.map((chunk) => {
493:       const position = unresolved.indexOf(chunk);
494:       // Lines are terminator-inclusive, so joining with '' reconstructs the exact text.
495:       const texts = chunkTexts(chunk, payload.base, payload.left, payload.right);
496:       const range = session!.store.centerRange(chunk.id);
497:       return {
498:         index: position + 1,
499:         chunkId: chunk.id,
500:         baseText: texts.base.join(''),
501:         leftText: texts.left.join(''),
502:         rightText: texts.right.join(''),
503:         resultStart: range.start,
504:         resultEnd: range.end,
505:       };
506:     }),
507:   };
508: }

663: /**
664:  * Places the AI's merged blocks into the result. Bottom-up by current position, so an
665:  * earlier replacement never shifts a later chunk's range mid-flight; chunks the user
666:  * decided while the request ran are left alone.
667:  */
668: function applyAiResolutions(
669:   resolutions: ReadonlyArray<{ chunkId: number; text: string }>,
670:   missing: number,
671: ): void {
672:   if (!session || !drawer) {
673:     return;
674:   }
675:   const { store } = session;
676:   const ordered = [...resolutions].sort(
677:     (a, b) => store.centerRange(b.chunkId).start - store.centerRange(a.chunkId).start,
678:   );
679:   let applied = 0;
680:   for (const resolution of ordered) {
681:     if (store.replaceText(resolution.chunkId, resolution.text)) {
682:       applied++;
683:     }
684:   }
685:   const remaining = session.chunks.filter(
686:     (c) => c.kind === 'conflict' && c.state === 'initial',
687:   ).length;
688:   drawer.showResolveReport(applied, resolutions.length + missing, remaining, fixAllMechanical);
689:   fixAllMechanical = 0;
690: }

692: /**
693:  * Builds (or rebuilds) the chunk model over the existing panes. Rebuilding happens when
694:  * the whitespace mode changes: the center resets to base and every decision starts over,
695:  * because chunks computed under one mode don't map onto ranges computed under another.
696:  */
697: function buildSession(whitespace: WhitespaceMode): void {
698:   if (!session) {
699:     return;
700:   }
701:   session.store.dispose();
702:   session.panes.center.getModel()?.setValue(session.payload.base);
703: 
704:   const chunks = computeChunks(session.payload.base, session.payload.left, session.payload.right, {
705:     whitespace,
706:   });
707:   session.chunks = chunks;
708:   session.whitespace = whitespace;
709:   session.wordRanges = computeWordRanges(chunks, session.payload);
710:   session.store = new ChunkStore(
711:     chunks,
712:     session.panes.center,
713:     session.payload.base,
714:     session.payload.left,
715:     session.payload.right,
716:     () => refresh(),
717:   );
718:   cursor = -1;
719:   session.currentChunkId = undefined;
720:   session.flashChunkId = undefined;
721:   lineNumbersSignature = '';
722:   // Chunk ids changed with the recompute; stale authorship must not mis-attach.
723:   session.authorChips.setData([]);
724:   refresh();
725:   requestBlame();
726: }

728: /** Asks an inline yes/no in the confirm bar; resolves false on cancel. */

734:       return;

736:     const finish = (answer: boolean) => {
737:       bar.classList.add('mf-hidden');
738:       bar.replaceChildren();
739:       resolve(answer);
740:     };
741:     const text = document.createElement('span');
742:     text.textContent = message;
743:     const yes = document.createElement('button');
744:     yes.textContent = 'Continue';
745:     yes.addEventListener('click', () => finish(true));
746:     const no = document.createElement('button');
747:     no.textContent = 'Cancel';
748:     no.addEventListener('click', () => finish(false));
749:     bar.replaceChildren(text, yes, no);
750:     bar.classList.remove('mf-hidden');
751:   });

```ts
const pushWords = (
  pane: 'left' | 'right',
  chunk: Chunk,
  ranges: readonly WordRange[] | undefined,
): void => {
  // Emphasis only helps while the chunk is still a live question.
```

This function only paints word-level highlights in the left/right side panes when `chunk.state === 'initial'`. When you accept a side (state becomes `appliedLeft`/`appliedRight`/`appliedBoth`), the word highlights in the side panes disappear.

Also note: the word highlights only paint on left/right panes, never on center. The comment says "The center shows the chunk's overall kind, since it holds the merged result."

The user wants: when they accept a side, keep the per-word highlight so they can still see the change points, so they can manually combine both sides.

Let me understand the user's scenario more precisely:
1. Two sides have word-level differences (e.g. left: `flex, flex-col`, right: `6xl, lg`).
2. The user accepts the left side into the center.
3. Now they want to also incorporate some of the right side's changes. But the word-level highlight is gone, so they can't see exactly which words differ.

So the request is essentially: don't hide the word-level emphasis once a chunk is resolved. Keep it visible (at least until the user manually edits or applies the merge, or keeps it through the whole session).

Wait, but let me think about what exactly they want to remain highlighted. There are a few interpretations:

1. Keep word highlights in the left/right side panes even after accepting (currently they disappear when state !== 'initial').
2. Additionally, add word highlights in the center pane showing where the center differs from the other side.

1: import type { Chunk, ChunkAction, ChunkState, Side } from './chunk';
2: import { transition } from './chunk';
3: import { splitLines } from './engine';
4: 
5: /**
6:  * Decides what text a chunk should contain after an action — the pure half of applying a
7:  * gutter button. The webview turns these into Monaco edits; keeping the decision here
8:  * means the interesting logic is testable without an editor.
9:  */
10: 
11: /** Text a chunk holds for a given state, given the three documents. */
12: export interface ChunkTexts {
13:   base: string[];
14:   left: string[];
15:   right: string[];
16: }
17: 
18: export function chunkTexts(chunk: Chunk, base: string, left: string, right: string): ChunkTexts {
19:   return {
20:     base: splitLines(base).slice(chunk.base.start, chunk.base.end),
21:     left: splitLines(left).slice(chunk.left.start, chunk.left.end),
22:     right: splitLines(right).slice(chunk.right.start, chunk.right.end),
23:   };
24: }
25: 
26: /**
27:  * The lines a chunk should contain in the result for a given state.
28:  *
29:  * `appliedBoth` concatenates in left-then-right order, matching how JetBrains stacks the
30:  * two sides when you accept both — and the order git would show them in a conflict block.
31:  */
32: export function textForState(texts: ChunkTexts, state: ChunkState): string[] {
33:   switch (state) {
34:     case 'appliedLeft':
35:       return texts.left;
36:     case 'appliedRight':
37:       return texts.right;
38:     case 'appliedBoth':
39:       return [...texts.left, ...texts.right];
40:     case 'initial':
41:     case 'ignored':
42:     case 'manuallyEdited':
43:       // Both keep whatever the result already holds: base for a fresh chunk, and for
44:       // 'ignored' that is precisely the point — deliberately take neither side.
45:       return texts.base;
46:   }
47: }
48: 
49: /** A resolved action: the new state plus the lines the result should now hold. */
50: export interface Resolution {
51:   state: ChunkState;
52:   lines: string[];
53: }
54: 
55: /**
56:  * Applies an action to a chunk, or returns null when the action isn't offered.
57:  * `manualEdit` is excluded: the text comes from the user, not from us.
58:  */
59: export function resolveAction(
60:   chunk: Chunk,
61:   texts: ChunkTexts,
62:   action: Exclude<ChunkAction, 'manualEdit'>,
63: ): Resolution | null {
64:   const next = transition(chunk.kind, chunk.state, action);
65:   if (next === null) {
66:     return null;
67:   }
68:   return { state: next, lines: textForState(texts, next) };
69: }
70: 
71: /** Whether a side's accept button should be shown for a chunk in its current state. */
72: export function canAccept(chunk: Chunk, side: Side): boolean {
73:   return (
74:     transition(chunk.kind, chunk.state, side === 'left' ? 'acceptLeft' : 'acceptRight') !== null
75:   );
76: }
77: 
78: export function canIgnore(chunk: Chunk): boolean {
79:   return transition(chunk.kind, chunk.state, 'ignore') !== null;
80: }
81: 
82: /**
83:  * The side each non-conflicting chunk should take for "Apply All Non-Conflicting Changes".
84:  * Conflicts are left alone — deciding those is the user's job.
85:  *
86:  * `only` restricts the sweep to one side, backing the left-only/right-only toolbar variants.
87:  */
88: export function nonConflictingAction(
89:   chunk: Chunk,
90:   only?: Side,
91: ): Exclude<ChunkAction, 'manualEdit'> | null {
92:   if (chunk.state !== 'initial') {
93:     return null;
94:   }
95:   switch (chunk.kind) {

Trong `webview/decorations.ts`, hàm tô highlight từng từ (`pushWords`) có điều kiện chặn:

```ts
// Emphasis only helps while the chunk is still a live question.

  return;
}
```

Tức là highlight từng từ **chỉ được vẽ khi chunk còn ở trạng thái `initial`**. Khi bạn accept một bên, trạng thái chuyển thành `appliedLeft`/`appliedRight`… nên toàn bộ highlight từng từ biến mất luôn.

## Cách sửa

1. **`webview/decorations.ts`** — bỏ điều kiện "chỉ khi initial". Giờ highlight từng từ được giữ lại cả sau khi đã quyết định, với 3 mức độ ([xem `wordTier`](webview/decorations.ts#L114)):
   - Bên **chưa quyết định** (vẫn còn nút accept/dismiss) → giữ **đậm như cũ**.

   - Bên **bị ignore/dismiss** → **mờ nhất** (đã chủ động bỏ qua).

## Kết quả với đúng ví dụ của bạn

Khi accept **trái** vào center:
- Bên trái (`flex, flex-col`) → mờ đi (đã accept).
- Bên phải (`6xl, lg`) → **vẫn giữ nguyên độ đậm**, để bạn nhìn rõ điểm khác và gõ/tách thêm từ bên phải vào center.

## Đã kiểm tra

- `pnpm run typecheck` ✅
- `pnpm run build` ✅ (bundle `dist/webview/main.js` + `main.css` đã được build lại)
- Test suite: 281 tests pass (chỉ có `activation.test.ts` fail trước đó vì thiếu `dist/extension.js` — giờ đã build nên pass).

Bạn chỉ cần **reload webview / mở lại merge editor** là thấy hiệu ứng mới (thay đổi nằm ở `dist/webview/main.js` đã build).

Lưu ý nhỏ: phần **center** hiện vẫn chỉ tô màu cả dòng chứ chưa tô từng từ. Nếu bạn muốn luôn cả highlight từng từ *trong pane center* (so center với bên chưa accept) thì đó là một thay đổi lớn hơn — mình có thể làm tiếp nếu bạn cần.

tools.name: ask_user_question
tools.description: Ask the user a concise question when you need confirmation, a choice, or missing information before proceeding.

options.description: Optional choices to show the user. If you recommend one, put it first and append "(Recommended)" to that label.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Managed `$DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Before any delete or move, verify that the resolved absolute target path is the intended one; never run it against a computed path you have not checked. An unset variable expands to an empty string, so guard variables in such paths with `${VAR:?}`. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap; on expiry the command moves to the background as a job instead of being killed.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact command the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create a persisted goal that keeps this session working across automatic continuation rounds. Use it when the direct human request is a long-running objective, even if the user did not say "goal"; not for single-turn work.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

sandbox_permissions.description: The narrowest wider sandbox mode for a one-shot retry of the exact operation the sandbox just denied; the retry asks the user for approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access. Use the language of the user’s current request.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current session goal, including the id and revision that update_goal requires.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files, not directories, whose paths match a glob pattern, including hidden and ignored files. Returns up to 100 paths in modification-time order; a larger result keeps the first paths and reports where the complete list was saved.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns up to 250 matches; a larger result reports where the complete match list was saved.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

tools.name: list_agents

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.description: Send a message to an agent. A working agent receives it at its next step; an idle agent starts a new turn with it. Returns delivery confirmation, not the agent's answer.

agent_id.description: The agent id of your direct continuable child, or your direct parent when you are a resident continuable child.

message.description: The message to deliver to the agent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for a skill. Call it before acting on a task that names or clearly matches a skill in the session skill catalog.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. It runs in the background by default and returns a subagent id you can continue with `send_message`; you are notified when the run settles.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Defaults to true. Set false only when your next action depends on the result.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. It runs in the background by default and returns a subagent id you can continue with `send_message`; you are notified when the run settles.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Defaults to true. Set false only when your next action depends on the result.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a task list to plan multi-step work and show progress; skip it for trivial single-step tasks. Add one todo per concrete step before you start. tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

So they want syntax/lint checking of the merged result in the center pane, showing errors/warnings (like diagnostics squiggles) so they can see if their merged result has syntax errors before applying.

This is a substantial feature. Let me think about how to implement it:

Options:
- **Option A**: Send the center content to the extension host, have the host compute diagnostics using the actual VS Code language services (e.g., by writing to a temp file and running `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics`, or by using a diagnostic provider). This gives real, language-aware lint (TypeScript/ESLint if configured). This is the "real" approach but complex and async.
- **Option B**: Use a JavaScript syntax parser (e.g., `@typescript-eslint/parser`, acorn, esprima) to parse the merged content and report syntax errors only. Simpler, works offline, but only for JS/TS (and maybe JSON/HTML via other parsers).
- **Option C**: Use Monaco's built-in tokenizer/validation? Monaco doesn't do full syntax validation out of the box for arbitrary content without a language worker configured.

The Monaco setup deliberately excludes the language services (ts/html/css/json workers) to keep the bundle small, with the comment "syntax highlighting is all a merge tool needs". So there's no built-in validation.

To implement syntax/lint checking of the center result, I have a few approaches. The cleanest that leverages VS Code's real diagnostics:

**Approach A: Extension host computes diagnostics via temp file + `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics`.**

The flow:
1. Webview sends the center content (debounced) to the host with the file's URI.
2. Host writes content to a temp file (or reuses a document) and calls `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics(uri)`.
3. Host sends back diagnostics (range + severity + message).
4. Webview sets Monaco markers on the center model.

This gives real lint (ESLint, TypeScript, etc.) as configured in the user's workspace. But it has complications: temp file needs a proper URI matching the workspace so the right extensions/TS project context applies; it's async; writing to disk repeatedly.

**Approach B: Do a pure syntax check in the webview using a JS parser.**

Use a lightweight parser. The project already has `diff` and `node-diff3` deps. For syntax checking, I could add a small parser dependency, but that's heavy and only covers JS/TS. Monaco doesn't have syntax validation bundled.

Actually, there's a simpler idea: **Monaco's own tokenizer can detect some syntax errors?** No, Monarch tokenizers are lexers, not parsers; they don't report syntax errors.

**Approach C: Use the extension host with the actual language services by creating an in-memory/untitled document.**

VS Code has `vscode.workspace.openTextDocument` with a `content` + `language` option that creates an untitled in-memory document, and `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics(uri)` works on it if a diagnostic provider (e.g., TypeScript language service, ESLint) is active. This is cleaner than writing to a temp file. But the untitled document's URI is `untitled:Untitled-N` with no workspace path, so TS project context / ESLint config resolution may not work properly. Also it won't be a "real" file path.

Actually, a more robust approach for TS: create an untitled doc but it won't map to tsconfig. Hmm.

Let me reconsider the scope. The user is asking for a "check syntax errors" / "check lint" feature. This is a feature request. Given the complexity and the multiple design choices with real tradeoffs, I should probably:

1. Ask a clarifying question about the scope/approach, OR
2. Propose a plan and implement a reasonable version.

Given the instruction about plan mode isn't active (I'm not in plan mode), and the user directly asked "được không" (can you?), I think the right move is to first understand feasibility and then either implement or ask.

Actually, let me reconsider. There's a genuinely simpler and very effective approach that fits this codebase well:

**Approach D: Use the extension host to run diagnostics against a temp file in the workspace, OR better — since the result will eventually be written to the actual conflicted file path — create a hidden temp file with the same basename/extension in the same directory (or use `vscode.workspace.openTextDocument` with a `file` scheme pointing to a temp file next to the original).**

Actually, the simplest robust approach that gives real lint: write the center content to a temp file **with the same extension, in the workspace** (or same directory), open it as a text document, request diagnostics from `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics()`, then clean up. For TS/ESLint this still may not match the project's config perfectly unless it's in the same directory tree.

This is getting complex. Let me step back and think about what delivers the most value with acceptable complexity.

Given the center content is the merged result, the most important thing is catching **syntax errors** (parse errors), because merging can easily produce invalid code (unbalanced braces, etc.). Real lint (unused vars, style) is less critical for a merge tool.

For syntax-only checking, I can do it **entirely in the webview** using Monaco's tokenizer? No.

Alternatively, do it in the **extension host** using VS Code's built-in capabilities: open the content as an in-memory document and ask for diagnostics. VS Code's TypeScript/JavaScript language feature extension will report **syntax errors** even for untitled documents (it uses the TS server, which parses without needing tsconfig for pure syntax). ESLint might not run without config. But syntax errors (parse errors) will be reported for `typescript`/`javascript` untitled docs.

Let me verify: `vscode.workspace.openTextDocument({ content, language: 'typescript' })` creates an untitled doc. `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics(uri)` returns diagnostics from providers registered for that language, including the built-in TS language features (which report semantic + syntactic errors). This works for JS/TS. For other languages (Python, JSON, HTML, CSS, etc.), VS Code has built-in providers too (JSON, HTML, CSS validation; Python needs the Python extension installed). This is actually a solid general approach.

The catch: `openTextDocument` with `{content, language}` creates an untitled doc with scheme `untitled`, and diagnostics from the TS server may take a moment (async). We'd need to poll or wait. Also, the untitled doc URI is stable per `openTextDocument` call (same content → same untitled doc? Actually each call may reuse). We'd need to manage closing it.

Hmm, but there's a subtlety: for TS/JS, the untitled doc's language id must be `typescript` or `javascript`, not just `typescriptreact` etc. The `languageId` from the host is derived from filename (e.g., `typescriptreact` for `.tsx`). We can pass that through.

Also `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics` returns synchronously current diagnostics; for a just-opened doc, the TS server hasn't produced them yet. We'd need to either:
- Use `vscode.workspace.onDidChangeDiagnostics` to wait for the specific URI, or
- Poll with a timeout.

This is doable but non-trivial and has edge cases.

Given all this complexity, I think the best course of action is to:
1. Ask the user a concise clarifying question about which approach they prefer (real workspace lint via extension host, vs. lightweight built-in syntax check), since it materially affects implementation and behavior.

Actually, wait — let me reconsider. The user has been asking in a fairly direct "can you do X" manner, and in the previous turn I just implemented. But this feature is much larger and has real design forks. The guidance says to use `ask_user_question` when I need a choice before proceeding.

Let me think about what's genuinely ambiguous:
1. **Scope**: syntax errors only (parse errors) vs full lint (ESLint/TS semantic diagnostics)?
2. **Where**: just the center pane (they said "ở center scene").
3. **Approach**: use VS Code's real language services (host round-trip) vs a bundled parser.

I think the cleanest, most valuable, and self-contained implementation is:

**Use VS Code's real diagnostics by round-tripping the center content through the host.** This gives true syntax errors for whatever language (as long as the user has the language extension), and even full lint if the language service provides it (ESLint via extension, TS semantic errors). It reuses the user's actual tooling, so it's genuinely "check lint".

But it's complex and I need to be careful. Let me look at how the host handles messages currently (MergePanel.ts) to understand where to hook in.

43: /**
44:  * One merge panel per conflicted file. Owns the webview lifecycle, loads the three
45:  * versions from git, and bridges messages; the merge UI itself lives in the webview.

47: export class MergePanel {

50:   private latestState: StatePayload | undefined;
51:   /** Cancels the in-flight AI explanation; recreated per request. */

58:   static async createOrShow(context: vscode.ExtensionContext, uri: vscode.Uri): Promise<void> {
59:     const key = uri.toString();
60:     const existing = MergePanel.panels.get(key);
61:     if (existing) {
62:       existing.panel.reveal();
63:       return;
64:     }
65: 
66:     const repoRoot = await findRepoRoot(uri.fsPath);
67:     if (!repoRoot) {
68:       void vscode.window.showErrorMessage('Merge Forge: this file is not inside a git repository.');
69:       return;
70:     }
71:     const relativePath = relative(repoRoot, uri.fsPath);
72: 
73:     let inputs: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof loadMergeInputs>>;
74:     try {
75:       inputs = await loadMergeInputs(repoRoot, relativePath, readEolSetting());
76:     } catch (error) {
77:       void vscode.window.showErrorMessage(
78:         `Merge Forge: ${error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)}`,
79:       );
80:       return;
81:     }
82: 
83:     if (inputs.unsupported) {
84:       await showUnsupported(inputs.unsupported, relativePath);
85:       return;
86:     }
87: 
88:     // Tab-title progress: "(2/5)" — position in the conflicted list at open time.
89:     const conflicted = await listConflicted(repoRoot).catch(() => [] as string[]);
90:     const position = conflicted.indexOf(relativePath) + 1;
91:     const progress =
92:       position > 0 && conflicted.length > 1 ? ` (${position}/${conflicted.length})` : '';
93:     const panel = vscode.window.createWebviewPanel(
94:       'mergeForge.mergeEditor',
95:       `Merge: ${relativePath}${progress}`,
96:       vscode.ViewColumn.Active,
97:       {
98:         enableScripts: true,
99:         // The center pane holds unsaved work; rebuilding it on every tab switch would lose it.
100:         retainContextWhenHidden: true,
101:         localResourceRoots: [vscode.Uri.joinPath(context.extensionUri, 'dist', 'webview')],
102:       },
103:     );
104: 
105:     const payload = {
106:       ...inputs.payload,
107:       filePath: relativePath,
108:       languageId: await detectLanguageId(uri),
109:       settings: { autoApplyNonConflicting: readAutoApply(), font: readEditorFont() },
110:     };
111:     // Fingerprint of the three inputs: stale saved work (index moved on) never matches.
112:     const inputsHash = createHash('sha1')
113:       .update(payload.base)
114:       .update('\0')
115:       .update(payload.left)
116:       .update('\0')
117:       .update(payload.right)
118:       .digest('hex');
119:     MergePanel.panels.set(
120:       key,
121:       new MergePanel(
122:         panel,
123:         context,
124:         key,
125:         uri,
126:         payload,
127:         repoRoot,
128:         relativePath,
129:         inputs.hadBom,
130:         inputsHash,
131:       ),
132:     );
133:   }

135:   /** Forwards a command to the focused merge panel, if there is one. */
136:   static runOnActive(action: MergeAction): void {
137:     for (const panel of MergePanel.panels.values()) {
138:       if (panel.panel.active) {
139:         panel.post({ type: 'runAction', action });
140:         return;

142:     }

145:   private constructor(
146:     private readonly panel: vscode.WebviewPanel,
147:     private readonly context: vscode.ExtensionContext,
148:     private readonly key: string,
149:     readonly uri: vscode.Uri,
150:     private readonly payload: InitPayload,
151:     private readonly repoRoot: string,
152:     private readonly relativePath: string,
153:     private readonly hadBom: boolean,
154:     private readonly inputsHash: string,
155:   ) {
156:     this.panel.webview.html = getWebviewHtml(this.panel.webview, context.extensionUri);
157:     this.panel.onDidDispose(() => {
158:       MergePanel.panels.delete(this.key);
159:       this.cancelExplain();
160:       void vscode.commands.executeCommand('setContext', 'mergeForge.panelFocused', false);
161:     });
162:     this.panel.onDidChangeViewState(() => {
163:       void vscode.commands.executeCommand(
164:         'setContext',
165:         'mergeForge.panelFocused',
166:         this.panel.active,
167:       );
168:     });
169:     this.panel.webview.onDidReceiveMessage((message: WebviewToHostMessage) =>
170:       this.onMessage(message),
171:     );
172:   }

174:   private post(message: HostToWebviewMessage): void {
175:     void this.panel.webview.postMessage(message);
176:   }

178:   private onMessage(message: WebviewToHostMessage): void {
179:     switch (message.type) {
180:       case 'ready': {
181:         this.post({ type: 'init', payload: this.payload });
182:         // Offer earlier unsaved work back — only when the inputs are byte-identical.
183:         const saved = this.context.workspaceState.get<StoredWork>(this.workKey());
184:         if (saved && saved.inputsHash === this.inputsHash) {
185:           this.post({ type: 'offerRestore', payload: saved.snapshot });
186:         }
187:         break;
188:       }
189:       case 'workSnapshot':
190:         void this.context.workspaceState.update(this.workKey(), {
191:           inputsHash: this.inputsHash,
192:           snapshot: message.payload,
193:           savedAt: Date.now(),
194:         } satisfies StoredWork);
195:         break;
196:       case 'discardWork':
197:         void this.context.workspaceState.update(this.workKey(), undefined);
198:         break;
199:       case 'state':
200:         this.latestState = message.payload;
201:         break;
202:       case 'abort':
203:         void this.abort();
204:         break;
205:       case 'log':
206:         // The output channel is where users can actually see this; console mirrors for dev.
207:         getOutputChannel().appendLine(
208:           `[${message.level}] ${this.relativePath}: ${message.message}`,
209:         );
210:         console[message.level === 'error' ? 'error' : 'warn'](`[merge-forge] ${message.message}`);
211:         break;
212:       case 'apply':
213:         void this.apply(message.payload.content, message.payload.eol);
214:         break;
215:       case 'explain':
216:         void this.explain(message.payload);
217:         break;
218:       case 'aiResolve':
219:         void this.aiResolve(message.payload.request, message.payload.explanation);
220:         break;
221:       case 'aiAsk':
222:         void this.aiAsk(message.payload.request, message.payload.history, message.payload.question);
223:         break;
224:       case 'explainCancel':
225:         this.cancelExplain();
226:         break;
227:       case 'openAiSetup':
228:         void vscode.commands.executeCommand('mergeForge.setApiKey');
229:         break;
230:       case 'blame':
231:         void this.blame(message.payload.ranges);
232:         break;
233:       case 'history':
234:         void this.sendHistory();
235:         break;
236:     }

239:   /**
240:    * Blames each conflict's side ranges against the side's committed rev. During a
241:    * rebase/cherry-pick git's incoming ref is what the left ("yours") pane shows —
242:    * the same swap `loadMergeInputs` applies to the pane contents.
243:    */
244:   private async blame(ranges: BlameRangeRequest[]): Promise<void> {
245:     try {
246:       const operation = await detectOperation(this.repoRoot);
247:       const incoming =
248:         operation.kind === 'cherry-pick'
249:           ? 'CHERRY_PICK_HEAD'
250:           : operation.kind === 'rebase'
251:             ? 'REBASE_HEAD'
252:             : 'MERGE_HEAD';
253:       const [leftRev, rightRev] = operation.swapPresentation
254:         ? [incoming, 'HEAD']
255:         : ['HEAD', incoming];
256:       const [left, right] = await Promise.all([
257:         blameRanges(
258:           this.repoRoot,
259:           leftRev,
260:           this.relativePath,
261:           ranges.map((r) => ({ start: r.leftStart, end: r.leftEnd })),
262:         ),
263:         blameRanges(
264:           this.repoRoot,
265:           rightRev,
266:           this.relativePath,
267:           ranges.map((r) => ({ start: r.rightStart, end: r.rightEnd })),
268:         ),
269:       ]);
270:       this.post({
271:         type: 'blameResult',
272:         payload: ranges.map((r, i) => ({
273:           chunkId: r.chunkId,
274:           ...(left.get(i) ? { left: left.get(i)! } : {}),
275:           ...(right.get(i) ? { right: right.get(i)! } : {}),
276:         })),
277:       });
278:     } catch {
279:       // Authorship is an enrichment — a failure just means no chips.
280:     }
281:   }

283:   private async sendHistory(): Promise<void> {
284:     try {
285:       if (!this.history) {
286:         const history = await fileHistory(this.repoRoot, this.relativePath);
287:         this.history = {
288:           entries: interleaveLanes(history.yours, history.theirs),
289:           ...(history.mergeBase ? { mergeBase: history.mergeBase } : {}),
290:           branches: {
291:             yours: this.payload.labels.left,
292:             theirs: this.payload.labels.right,
293:           },
294:         };
295:       }
296:       this.post({ type: 'historyData', payload: this.history });
297:     } catch {
298:       this.post({
299:         type: 'historyData',
300:         payload: {
301:           entries: [],
302:           branches: { yours: this.payload.labels.left, theirs: this.payload.labels.right },
303:         },
304:       });
305:     }
306:   }

308:   /** The streaming callbacks every drawer-bound request shares. */
309:   private drawerCallbacks(): {
310:     onDelta(text: string): void;
311:     onActivity(text: string): void;
312:     onDone(truncated?: boolean): void;
313:     onError(message: string): void;
314:   } {
315:     return {
316:       onDelta: (text) => this.post({ type: 'explainDelta', text }),
317:       onActivity: (text) => this.post({ type: 'explainActivity', text }),
318:       onDone: (truncated) =>
319:         this.post({ type: 'explainDone', ...(truncated ? { truncated: true } : {}) }),
320:       onError: (message) => this.post({ type: 'explainError', message }),
321:     };
322:   }

324:   /** Streams an AI explanation of the file's conflicts back into the webview drawer. */
325:   private async explain(request: ExplainRequest): Promise<void> {
326:     const started = await this.startAiRequest(STEP_BUDGET_EXPLAIN);
327:     if (!started) {
328:       return;
329:     }
330:     await started.provider.stream(
331:       buildExplainPrompt(request, started.context),
332:       this.drawerCallbacks(),
333:       started.token,
334:       started.tools,
335:     );
336:   }

338:   /**
339:    * "Resolve with AI": one request returns machine-parsed merged blocks; only what
340:    * parses is sent back — a skipped or garbled block just leaves that conflict open.
341:    * One automatic retry covers indexes the first answer missed or garbled.
342:    */
343:   private async aiResolve(request: ExplainRequest, explanation?: string): Promise<void> {
344:     const started = await this.startAiRequest(STEP_BUDGET_RESOLVE);
345:     if (!started) {
346:       return;
347:     }
348:     const base = buildResolvePrompt(request, explanation, started.context);
349:     const collected = new Map<number, string>();
350:     const expected = request.conflicts.map((c) => c.index);
351: 
352:     const postResolutions = (): void => {
353:       const resolutions = request.conflicts
354:         .filter((c) => collected.has(c.index))
355:         .map((c) => ({ chunkId: c.chunkId, text: collected.get(c.index)! }));
356:       this.post({
357:         type: 'aiResolutions',
358:         resolutions,
359:         missing: request.conflicts.length - resolutions.length,
360:       });
361:     };
362: 
363:     const attempt = async (prompt: PromptPair, isRetry: boolean): Promise<void> => {
364:       let accumulated = '';
365:       await started.provider.stream(
366:         prompt,
367:         {
368:           ...this.drawerCallbacks(),
369:           onDelta: (text) => {
370:             accumulated += text;
371:           },
372:           onDone: () => {
373:             for (const [index, text] of parseResolutions(accumulated, expected)) {
374:               if (!collected.has(index)) {
375:                 collected.set(index, text);
376:               }
377:             }
378:             const missing = expected.filter((i) => !collected.has(i));
379:             if (missing.length === 0 || isRetry || started.token.isCancellationRequested) {
380:               postResolutions();
381:               return;
382:             }
383:             this.post({
384:               type: 'explainActivity',
385:               text: `⚙ Retrying ${missing.length} unparsed conflict${missing.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}`,
386:             });
387:             void attempt(
388:               { system: base.system, user: `${base.user}\n\n${buildRetryAddendum(missing)}` },
389:               true,
390:             );
391:           },
392:         },
393:         started.token,
394:         started.tools,
395:       );
396:     };
397:     await attempt(base, false);
398:   }

400:   /** The drawer's follow-up chat — answers stream over the explain channel. */
401:   private async aiAsk(
402:     request: ExplainRequest,
403:     history: Array<{ question: string; answer: string }>,
404:     question: string,
405:   ): Promise<void> {

409:     }

412:       this.drawerCallbacks(),
413:       started.token,
414:       started.tools,
415:     );

418:   /**
419:    * Shared preamble: cancel any in-flight request, resolve the backend (or report
420:    * setup), and assemble the request's context — branch intent for the prompt,
421:    * tool executors when the backend can honor them.
422:    */
423:   private async startAiRequest(stepBudget: number): Promise<
424:     | {
425:         provider: Exclude<ExplainProvider, { kind: 'unconfigured' }>;
426:         token: vscode.CancellationToken;
427:         context: PromptContext;
428:         tools: StreamToolOptions | undefined;
429:       }
430:     | undefined
431:   > {
432:     this.cancelExplain();
433:     const cancellation = new vscode.CancellationTokenSource();
434:     this.explainCancellation = cancellation;
435:     const provider = await getExplainProvider(this.context);
436:     if (provider.kind === 'unconfigured') {
437:       this.post({
438:         type: 'explainError',
439:         message: 'No AI backend is configured.',
440:         unconfigured: true,
441:       });
442:       return undefined;
443:     }
444:     if (cancellation.token.isCancellationRequested) {
445:       return undefined;
446:     }
447:     this.subjects ??= await branchSubjects(this.repoRoot).catch(() => ({
448:       yours: [],
449:       theirs: [],
450:     }));
451:     const context: PromptContext = {
452:       subjects: this.subjects,
453:       toolsAvailable: provider.supportsTools,
454:     };
455:     const tools = provider.supportsTools
456:       ? { executors: createToolExecutors(this.repoRoot), stepBudget }
457:       : undefined;
458:     return { provider, token: cancellation.token, context, tools };
459:   }

461:   private cancelExplain(): void {
462:     this.explainCancellation?.cancel();
463:     this.explainCancellation?.dispose();
464:     this.explainCancellation = undefined;
465:   }
466: 
467:   /**
468:    * Writes the result and marks the file resolved.
469:    *
470:    * Applying with conflicts still untouched would stage a file containing the base text
471:    * where a decision belonged — quietly discarding both sides' work — so that needs an
472:    * explicit confirmation rather than a silent success.
473:    */
474:   private async apply(content: string, eol: Eol): Promise<void> {
475:     const unresolved = this.latestState?.unresolvedConflicts ?? 0;
476:     if (unresolved > 0) {
477:       const proceed = await vscode.window.showWarningMessage(
478:         `${unresolved} conflict${unresolved === 1 ? '' : 's'} in "${this.relativePath}" ${
479:           unresolved === 1 ? 'is' : 'are'
480:         } still unresolved. Applying now keeps the original version for ${
481:           unresolved === 1 ? 'it' : 'them'
482:         }.`,
483:         { modal: true },
484:         'Apply Anyway',
485:       );
486:       if (proceed !== 'Apply Anyway') {
487:         this.post({ type: 'applyResult', ok: false, error: 'cancelled' });
488:         return;
489:       }
490:     }
491: 
492:     try {
493:       await applyResolved(this.repoRoot, this.relativePath, content, eol, this.hadBom);
494:       // The work is in git now; the crash-safety copy would only offer stale state.
495:       await this.context.workspaceState.update(this.workKey(), undefined);
496:     } catch (error) {
497:       const detail = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
498:       this.post({ type: 'applyResult', ok: false, error: detail });
499:       void vscode.window.showErrorMessage(`Merge Forge: could not apply — ${detail}`);
500:       return;
501:     }
502: 
503:     this.panel.dispose();
504:     await this.reportProgress();
505:   }

507:   /** Tells the user where the merge stands, and keeps the loop going to the next file. */
508:   private async reportProgress(): Promise<void> {
509:     const remaining = await listConflicted(this.repoRoot).catch(() => undefined);
510:     if (remaining === undefined) {
511:       return;
512:     }
513:     if (remaining.length === 0) {
514:       void vscode.window.showInformationMessage(
515:         `Resolved "${this.relativePath}" — all conflicts resolved, ready to commit.`,
516:       );
517:       return;
518:     }
519:     const next = vscode.Uri.file(join(this.repoRoot, remaining[0]!));
520:     if (readAutoAdvance()) {
521:       // Keyboard-driven loop: straight into the next conflicted file, no stop.
522:       await vscode.commands.executeCommand('mergeForge.resolveThis', next);
523:       return;
524:     }
525:     const choice = await vscode.window.showInformationMessage(
526:       `Resolved "${this.relativePath}" — ${remaining.length} conflicted file${
527:         remaining.length === 1 ? '' : 's'
528:       } left.`,
529:       'Next Conflict',
530:     );
531:     if (choice === 'Next Conflict') {
532:       await vscode.commands.executeCommand('mergeForge.resolveThis', next);
533:     }
534:   }
535: 
536:   /** Closes without touching the conflicted file, so the merge can be restarted. */
537:   private async abort(): Promise<void> {
538:     if (this.latestState?.dirty) {
539:       const discard = await vscode.window.showWarningMessage(
540:         `Discard your work on "${this.relativePath}"? The file keeps its conflict markers.`,
541:         { modal: true },
542:         'Discard',
543:       );
544:       if (discard !== 'Discard') {
545:         return;
546:       }
547:       // An explicit discard should not resurrect as a restore offer next time.
548:       await this.context.workspaceState.update(this.workKey(), undefined);
549:     }
550:     this.panel.dispose();
551:   }
552: 
553:   private workKey(): string {
554:     return `mergeForge.work.${this.relativePath}`;
555:   }
556: }
557: 
558: /** What crash-safety persists per file: the snapshot plus its validity fingerprint. */
559: interface StoredWork {
560:   inputsHash: string;
561:   snapshot: WorkSnapshot;
562:   savedAt: number;
563: }
564: 
565: function readEolSetting(): EolSetting {
566:   const value = vscode.workspace.getConfiguration('mergeForge').get<string>('lineEnding', 'auto');
567:   return value === 'lf' || value === 'crlf' ? value : 'auto';
568: }
569: 
570: function readAutoApply(): boolean {
571:   return vscode.workspace
572:     .getConfiguration('mergeForge')
573:     .get<boolean>('autoApplyNonConflicting', false);
574: }
575: 
576: function readAutoAdvance(): boolean {
577:   return vscode.workspace.getConfiguration('mergeForge').get<boolean>('autoAdvance', false);
578: }
579: 
580: /** The user's editor font — the panes should feel like their editor, not ours. */
581: function readEditorFont(): { size: number; family: string; ligatures: boolean } {
582:   const editor = vscode.workspace.getConfiguration('editor');
583:   return {
584:     size: editor.get<number>('fontSize', 12),
585:     family: editor.get<string>('fontFamily', ''),
586:     ligatures: editor.get<boolean | string>('fontLigatures', false) === true,

599: /**
600:  * A delete/modify conflict has nothing to show in three panes — one side has no file at
601:  * all — so offer the only two decisions that exist instead of an empty editor.

603: async function showUnsupported(reason: UnsupportedReason, relativePath: string): Promise<void> {
604:   if (reason === 'binary') {

613:       `Merge Forge: "${relativePath}" is over 10 MB — too large for the visual merge editor. ` +
614:         'Resolve it in a plain editor or from the command line.',
615:     );
616:     return;
617:   }
618:   const deletedBy = reason === 'deletedByThem' ? 'the incoming branch' : 'your branch';

166: fn parse_positionals<I>(args: I) -> Parsed

177:         [] => Parsed::Usage,
178:         [merged] => Parsed::Git {
179:             merged: PathBuf::from(merged),
180:         },
181:         [local, remote, base, merged] => Parsed::Files {
182:             local: PathBuf::from(local),
183:             remote: PathBuf::from(remote),
184:             base: PathBuf::from(base),
185:             merged: PathBuf::from(merged),
186:         },
187:         other => Parsed::Invalid(format!(
188:             "Expected 4 paths ($LOCAL $REMOTE $BASE $MERGED) or 1 conflicted file.\n\nReceived:\n{}",
189:             other.join("\n")

240: fn load_git(merged: &Path) -> Launch {

263:     } else {
264:         (stages.ours, stages.theirs)

269:         ));

274:         ));
275:     };
276:     let base = stages.base.unwrap_or_default();
277:     let labels = branch_labels_for(&root, &operation);
278:     finish(
279:         merged,
280:         Some(root),
281:         Some(relative),
282:         &yours,
283:         &base,

295: fn read_stages(root: &Path, relative: &str) -> Result<Stages, String> {
296:     let listing = git_text(root, &["ls-files", "-u", "--", relative])?;
297:     if listing.trim().is_empty() {
298:         return Err(format!(
299:             "{relative} is not conflicted.\n\nOpen it from Fork while a merge, rebase, or cherry-pick is in progress."
300:         ));
301:     }
302:     let mut stages = Stages {
303:         base: None,
304:         ours: None,
305:         theirs: None,
306:     };
307:     for line in listing.lines() {
308:         let Some((meta, _)) = line.split_once('\t') else {
309:             continue;
310:         };
311:         let mut parts = meta.split_whitespace();
312:         let sha = parts.nth(1);
313:         let stage = parts.next();
314:         let (Some(sha), Some(stage)) = (sha, stage) else {
315:             continue;
316:         };
317:         let blob = git_bytes(root, &["cat-file", "blob", sha])?;
318:         match stage {
319:             "1" => stages.base = Some(blob),
320:             "2" => stages.ours = Some(blob),
321:             "3" => stages.theirs = Some(blob),
322:             _ => {}
323:         }
324:     }
325:     Ok(stages)
326: }

364:             .or_else(|| read_git_file(root, "rebase-apply/head-name"))
365:             .map(|name| ref_to_branch(&name))
366:             .unwrap_or_else(|| "Yours".into());

369:             .filter(|name| !name.is_empty())
370:             .unwrap_or_else(|| "upstream".into());
371:         return Labels {
372:             left: yours,
373:             right: theirs,
374:         };
375:     }
376:     let yours = git_text(root, &["branch", "--show-current"])
377:         .ok()
378:         .filter(|name| !name.is_empty())
379:         .unwrap_or_else(|| "Yours".into());
380:     let incoming = if operation.kind == "cherry-pick" {
381:         "CHERRY_PICK_HEAD"
382:     } else {
383:         "MERGE_HEAD"
384:     };
385:     let theirs = git_text(root, &["name-rev", "--name-only", incoming])
386:         .ok()
387:         .filter(|name| !name.is_empty() && name != "undefined")
388:         .unwrap_or_else(|| "Theirs".into());

408:     let remote = match decode_side(remote, "remote") {
409:         Ok(text) => text,

412:     let base = match decode_side(base, "base") {

458: fn decode_side(bytes: &[u8], label: &str) -> Result<Decoded, String> {
459:     if looks_binary(bytes) {
460:         return Err(format!(
461:             "the {label} side is binary — Merge Forge only opens text files"
462:         ));
463:     }
464:     if bytes.len() > MAX_BYTES {
465:         return Err(format!("the {label} side is over 10 MB"));
466:     }
467:     let had_bom = bytes.starts_with(&[0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF]);
468:     let raw = if had_bom { &bytes[3..] } else { bytes };
469:     let text =
470:         String::from_utf8(raw.to_vec()).map_err(|_| format!("the {label} side is not UTF-8"))?;
471:     Ok(Decoded { text, had_bom })
472: }

474: fn looks_binary(bytes: &[u8]) -> bool {
475:     bytes.iter().take(8000).any(|byte| *byte == 0)
476: }

478: fn detect_eol(text: &str) -> Eol {
479:     let mut crlf = 0;
480:     let mut lf = 0;
481:     let bytes = text.as_bytes();
482:     for (index, byte) in bytes.iter().enumerate() {
483:         if *byte == b'\n' {
484:             if index > 0 && bytes[index - 1] == b'\r' {
485:                 crlf += 1;
486:             } else {
487:                 lf += 1;
488:             }
489:         }
490:     }
491:     if crlf > lf {
492:         Eol::Crlf
493:     } else {
494:         Eol::Lf
495:     }
496: }

499:     text.replace("\r\n", "\n")

502: fn encode_result(content: &str, eol: &str, had_bom: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
503:     let without_bom = content.strip_prefix('\u{feff}').unwrap_or(content);
504:     let text = if eol.eq_ignore_ascii_case("crlf") {
505:         without_bom.replace('\n', "\r\n")
506:     } else {
507:         without_bom.to_string()
508:     };
509:     let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(text.len() + 3);
510:     if had_bom {
511:         out.extend_from_slice(&[0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF]);
512:     }
513:     out.extend_from_slice(text.as_bytes());
514:     out
515: }

530:         "toml" => "toml",
531:         "sh" | "bash" | "zsh" => "shell",
532:         "vue" => "html",
533:         _ => "plaintext",
534:     }
